entries.title: Contacts: dropdown fields from imports now filter and fill in correctly
entries.summary: Dropdown and multi-select fields whose options came from an import or an older setup now behave like any other field. Filtering on one of them returns every contact whose cell shows that option, and in **New Contact Details** picking one option selects only that option.

where.path: Contacts → All Contacts → Filter / Add Contact

entries.use_case: If your team imported contact fields such as an event status or an attendance list, filters on those fields now include every matching contact, and adding a contact by hand lets you pick a single option instead of all of them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a dropdown filter misses contacts whose cell shows the value, or that picking one option in Add Contact selects them all or doesn't stick.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with dropdown fields created by import (SB-11729, SB-11730, SB-11731).
internal.gotchas: Affects fields whose options have no id (imports, older fields). Fields created in the UI were never affected.

entries.title: Caption and text track actions now appear in History
entries.summary: Adding, editing, removing, or requesting generated captions on a media item or session file now creates a **History** row. Each row shows one of four labels — **Added a text track**, **Edited a text track**, **Requested generated captions**, or **Removed a text track** — along with the track's kind and label as detail.
entries.use_case: Teams managing accessibility or localisation for session recordings can now audit exactly when captions were added, changed, or generated — and by whom — without relying on manual notes or external tracking.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to audit caption or text track changes on session files or media items.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Media add-on or session file captions who needs an audit trail of accessibility-related changes.
internal.gotchas: History rows for text track actions taken before this fix were silently dropped and cannot be recovered retroactively.
internal.talk_track: Every time someone adds, edits, removes, or requests generated captions on a session file, a timestamped History row now records it — so you always know who changed what and when.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that caption and text track actions (add, edit, remove, generate) are recorded in the session file History tab, with the track kind and label shown as detail.

entries.title: Reviewer email log loads again in evaluation plans
entries.summary: Opening the **Email Log** from the **Reviewers** list in an evaluation plan now loads correctly and lists each send with its delivery status (Delivered, Opened, Bounced, and so on). Previously, every attempt to open the log returned a server error.
entries.use_case: Admins running a review cycle who need to confirm that reviewer invitation or reminder emails were delivered — or to investigate why a reviewer says they never received one — can now open the email log and see the delivery status for every send without hitting a server error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that reviewers are not receiving emails and the admin cannot check the email log, or when a customer mentions a server error on the Reviewers email log.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using evaluation plans who sends emails to reviewers.
internal.gotchas: The fix was validated with a unit test mocking the database; no integration DB test was run, so confirm in production if a customer reports a lingering issue.
internal.talk_track: The reviewer email log is working again — you can open it from the Reviewers step of any evaluation plan to see exactly which emails were delivered, opened, or bounced.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the Email Log is accessible from the Reviewers step and explain what delivery statuses (Delivered, Opened, Bounced, etc.) mean in that context.

entries.title: Merge Duplicates compare step keeps all contact columns visible
entries.summary: In the **Merge Duplicates** compare step, a contact with a long field value (such as a lengthy **Biography**) no longer pushes other contact columns off screen. The table now divides column width equally across contacts, wraps long values to three lines, and shows the full text in a tooltip on hover.
entries.use_case: When reviewing duplicate contacts that have long biography or notes fields, organizers can now see all candidate contacts side by side without any columns being pushed off screen, making it straightforward to choose which values to keep before merging.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports that the Merge Duplicates compare view appeared to show only one contact, or that columns were missing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer who uses the duplicate-merge workflow on contacts with long text fields such as Biography.
internal.gotchas: The fix was validated with jsdom unit tests only; layout was not verified in a real browser, though the Tailwind classes used (table-fixed, line-clamp-3, break-words) are standard and well-supported.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note explaining that the compare table shows all contacts side by side with long values truncated to three lines and the full text available on hover.

entries.title: New "Cinematic · film" animated card is the default for individual Advocacy cards
entries.summary: A new **Cinematic · film** animated card style is now the default for individual Advocacy cards — speakers, exhibitors, sponsors and attendees. The 15.9-second film opens with a light flare, moves through an identity beat (headshot, name, title, company, event logo), a role lead-in ("SPEAKING AT" / "EXHIBITING AT" / …), a particle-burst logo reveal, and closes with city, dates and venue — all tinted to the event's brand colours. Session cards keep their own presets. Layout sliders are hidden for this variant.
entries.use_case: Organizers who want a polished, cinematic social video for every speaker, exhibitor, sponsor or attendee get a branded 15.9-second film automatically — no design work required. The film adapts to any event's brand colours and logo, so it works out of the box for any event.

cs_action.note: The PR author notes the Remotion bundle uploads on deploy but the film was not tested in a running Quick Launch / Advocacy flow on dev. Confirm the bundle is live in production before telling customers the new default is active.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about Advocacy animated cards, speaker social sharing, or wants a more polished video asset for their event without custom production.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy animated cards for speakers, exhibitors, sponsors or attendees — especially those who previously used the older default card style.
internal.gotchas: Session cards are unaffected and keep their own presets. Layout sliders are hidden for the Cinematic variant — customers who relied on layout adjustments will not see those controls for individual cards. The film was tested locally against a single fixture (Northwind) and not in a live Quick Launch flow; watch for rendering issues in production.
internal.talk_track: Your speakers, exhibitors and attendees now get a cinematic 15.9-second branded video automatically when they share their Advocacy card — light flare, their headshot and name, a 'Speaking At' reveal, your logo, and a closing city/dates card, all in your event's colours. No design work needed.

draft.docs_gap: The Advocacy campaigns guide should add a section describing the Cinematic · film animated card variant — its timeline beats, how it inherits brand colours and logo, which audience types it applies to (speakers, exhibitors, sponsors, attendees but not sessions), and that layout sliders are hidden for this variant.
draft.why_use_it: Advocacy animated cards let speakers, exhibitors, sponsors and attendees share a short branded video on social media to promote the event. The Cinematic · film style produces a professional, broadcast-quality sequence — light flare, identity reveal, role lead-in, logo burst and a closing city/dates card — all generated from the event's own brand colours and logo. Because the film is procedurally generated, it works for any event without custom video production.

entries.title: New "Speakers to tag" page to identify and assign unnamed voices and unmatched recordings in bulk
entries.summary: A new **Speakers to tag** tab in the Media nav (with a count badge) surfaces all unnamed voices and recordings without a session in one place. The **Voices** tab lists each unidentified voice with talk time, a sample play button, and a suggested speaker with confidence level; per-row **Accept**, **Pick** and **Not a speaker** actions, plus bulk **Accept suggestions**, **Accept all high-confidence suggestions** and CSV export, let organizers clear the queue quickly. The **Recordings without a session** tab shows suggested session matches with the same accept/pick workflow. Warning notices also appear on the Library and Clips pages when gaps remain.
entries.use_case: Event teams that use Voices to auto-generate speaker clips and quotes can now resolve all unnamed voices and unmatched recordings from a single page instead of opening each recording individually — saving significant time after a multi-session event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Voices or Transcribe asks how to efficiently attribute clips and quotes to speakers after a multi-session event, or when they complain about having to open each recording individually to name voices.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer with the Media / Voices feature who records multi-session events and relies on speaker attribution for clips and quotes.
internal.gotchas: The PR notes it was not clicked through in a browser against a running API — playback of presigned recording URLs and keyboard flow inside popovers were verified only through tests and code review. Confirm the API side (sessionboard-web-api#5573) is also deployed before telling customers the feature is live. Short untagged voices under 30 seconds are counted but not listed as rows.
internal.talk_track: After your event, head to Media → Speakers to tag. Every unnamed voice is listed with a suggested speaker and a confidence score — hit Accept all high-confidence suggestions and the system assigns them in one go, so your clips and quotes are attributed instantly without opening a single recording.

draft.docs_gap: The share-clips guide should add a "Speakers to tag" section explaining the two tabs (Voices and Recordings without a session), how confidence levels work, the bulk-accept actions, the count badge in the nav, and the warning notices on the Library and Clips pages.
draft.why_use_it: The Speakers to tag page collects every unresolved voice and every recording that has not yet been linked to a session, so organizers can work through the full backlog in one place. Suggested speakers are shown with a confidence rating and a reason, and a single click accepts the suggestion or opens a picker to choose someone else. Bulk actions — including accepting all high-confidence suggestions at once — let teams clear a large event's worth of recordings in minutes rather than hours, ensuring that clips and quotes are attributed to the right speakers as soon as possible.

entries.title: Send speakers, sponsors and teammates their clips in one step — with an audit trail and results rollup
entries.summary: Organizers can now send every speaker, sponsor/exhibitor contact and teammate a personal link to their own clip gallery in a single send from **Media → Clip Share**. The gallery is paged (no 60-clip cap), groups clips by session, and respects per-clip **Hide** toggles. A **Plan** dry run shows who will receive a link, who is skipped and why, and which sessions have no clips yet. After sending, the **Results** view (by person or by clip, exportable as CSV) shows opens and engagement. Each send, hide and track action is written to the audit trail under the **media_clip_share** subject.
entries.use_case: After a conference, an organizer can send every speaker a personal link to their own session clips in one click — no campaign setup required. Speakers land on a paged gallery scoped to their sessions, and the organizer can see who opened their link and which clips were viewed from the Results tab.

cs_action.note: This is a net-new surface (Media → Clip Share) that requires the Media add-on. Proactively show it to any customer who has Media and regularly shares clips with speakers post-event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to get clips to speakers after an event, or when they are frustrated by the 60-clip cap or the need to build an Advocacy campaign just to share recordings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any platform customer with the Media add-on who produces clips and wants to share them with speakers, sponsors or teammates without a full Advocacy campaign.
internal.gotchas: The hidden-clip toggle (GET|PUT …/clip-share/hidden) is per-clip and per-event; clips hidden here do not affect the main Clips library or Advocacy campaigns. Advocacy lists filter on source='advocacy', so clip-share sends never appear in Advocacy campaign lists. Resending reuses existing recipient rows and skips already-emailed people unless the resend flag is set. The migrations were not run against a local DB during development — confirm they ran cleanly in staging before announcing GA.
internal.talk_track: After your event, go to Media → Clip Share, run the Plan to see who gets what, hide any clips you're not ready to share, then hit Send. Every speaker gets a personal link to their own clips — no campaign needed. You can see who opened their gallery and which clips they watched right from the Results tab.

draft.docs_gap: The /marketing/share-clips guide should be updated to document the new Clip Share flow: the Plan dry-run (skipped recipients and why, unassigned sessions), the per-clip Hide toggle, the Send step (speakers get a personal /clips/:token link via Dispatch, opt-outs honoured), the paged gallery recipients see (grouped by session, no cap), the Results view (by person or by clip, CSV export), and the audit trail entries written under the media_clip_share subject.
draft.why_use_it: Clip Share lets you deliver each speaker, sponsor and teammate a personal gallery of the clips that belong to them — without building an Advocacy campaign or manually picking clips. Because each link is scoped to the recipient's sessions and account, speakers see only their own content, sponsors see only their brand's clips, and you stay in control with per-clip hide toggles. Engagement is tracked per person and per clip so you know who watched and can follow up with confidence.

entries.title: Review, score and decide on applications with a dedicated dashboard, review plan and decision emails
entries.summary: Application forms now have a full review workflow behind the **Applications Review** feature flag. Organizers choose a **Submission Setup** type (**Contacts** or **Attendees**) when creating a form, configure a review plan from the **Review** tab (rounds, reviewers, blind review, sensitive-field privacy), score submissions in the **Submissions** table, and issue **Accept in full / Partial / Decline** decisions with optional amounts. Accepted and declined submissions move to queues; clicking **Send decision emails** notifies applicants. Attendees who applied see their decision (**Under review / Accepted / Declined**) on a dedicated public page. An **Applications** column also appears in **CRM → People → Attendees** when an attendee application form exists for the event.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Applications Review; then Event → Applications → [Form] → Review

where.path: Event → Applications → [Form] → Dashboard / Submissions / Review / Audit log

entries.use_case: Event teams running grant programs, scholarship applications, or attendee-facing calls can now collect, score and decide on applications in one place — complete with blind review, round-based scoring, partial-award amounts, and automated decision emails — without leaving Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The entire review workflow is behind the super-user flag plus the event feature `applications_review`. Both must be on before any of these screens are visible to the customer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to run a grant, scholarship, award, or attendee application process with scoring and decision notifications inside Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running structured application programs — grants, scholarships, speaker fellowships, attendee applications — who need a review committee and formal accept/decline communications.
internal.staff_path: Event → Applications → [Form] → Review tab (plan wizard); Submissions tab (scoring panel, decision queues, Send decision emails button)
internal.gotchas: Audit log endpoint and some review/decision API payloads are listed as TO BUILD in the backend contract; those screens show loading/empty/error states until the API lands. The feature has not yet been walked end-to-end in a browser as of merge. Attendees have no speaker portal Applications card — their decision page is a standalone public URL, not a portal task.
internal.talk_track: You can now run your entire application review inside Sessionboard: build the form, set up a blind multi-round review with your committee, score each submission, and send accept or decline emails with a single click. Attendee applicants see their decision on a dedicated page the moment you send it.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add sections covering: (1) choosing Contacts vs. Attendees submission type and why it can't be changed after creation; (2) marking questions as sensitive and how that affects reviewer visibility; (3) the Review tab — creating a plan, configuring blind review, rounds and personas; (4) the Submissions table columns (Registration status, Round, Score, Amount awarded) and the submission panel (answers, scores, accept-in-full / partial / decline with amount); (5) the Accept Queue and Decline Queue and how Send decision emails works; (6) the applicant-facing decision page for attendees; and (7) the Applications column in CRM → People → Attendees.
draft.why_use_it: Applications in Sessionboard lets you collect structured submissions from contacts or attendees, route them through a scored review process, and communicate decisions back to applicants automatically. You control who sees sensitive answers, how many review rounds to run, and whether reviewers see applicant names. Because decisions, scores and emails all live in the same form dashboard, your team spends less time coordinating across spreadsheets and email threads.

entries.title: History, undo, a "details updated" email, readable version labels, and review sharing for field events and Marketing pages
entries.summary: Organizers can now view a change history for event basics and the registration form on a field event, and restore any earlier state with one click (**Restore**). A new **Details Updated** email lets marketers notify registered guests about what changed — with a preview step before anything sends. Site version history now shows a plain **label**, the author's name, and which version is **Live**. Individual draft edits within an AI run can be undone separately, and any two versions can be compared with a diff view. The **Share for Review** link now works on event pages and block Sites, with an optional **Approve** step that records who signed off and which draft revision they approved.

where.path: Marketing → Events → [Field Event] → History / Details Updated / Share for Review

entries.use_case: Tour and field-event marketers who update event details after registration opens can now send a targeted "details updated" email to confirmed guests — previewing the audience count and a rendered sample before it goes out — and can undo any accidental change to event basics or the registration form without contacting support. Teams that use AI to build pages can share a review link with a named teammate, get a formal approval recorded against the exact draft revision, and compare any two versions side by side.

cs_action.note: Multiple companion PRs (public-api route allow-list, mcp-server tools, sessionboard-docs) are required for the full feature surface to be live; confirm all are merged and deployed before promoting to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running multi-city tours or field events asks how to communicate last-minute venue or schedule changes to registered guests, or when they want an audit trail and undo for event configuration changes.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing customers running field events or tours, especially those using AI assistants to build and iterate on event pages and who need a formal review/approval workflow before publishing.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Events → [Field Event] → History; Marketing → Events → [Field Event] → Details Updated; Site Builder → Versions; Site Builder → Share for Review
internal.gotchas: The DB migration (20261227100000-create-event-setting-changes) must run in each environment before history writes appear. The 'Details Updated' email uses a new gathering key (gathering-details-updated) and is never auto-scheduled — a human must explicitly call /send with confirmed: true. Draft-step history keeps only the newest 20 edits per run. Review approval records the server's draft revision at approval time; if the draft is edited after approval, the approval is against the older revision.
internal.talk_track: If you update the venue or time for a tour stop after people have already registered, you can now send a 'Details Updated' email directly from Sessionboard — it shows you exactly who will get it and what it looks like before you send. And if anyone on your team makes a change by mistake, just open History and hit Restore.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add sections covering: (1) how to open and use the event-settings change history and restore an earlier state; (2) how to preview and send the Details Updated email, including the audience-count preview and the confirmed send step; (3) how readable version labels, author names, and the Live indicator appear in site version history; (4) how to compare two versions with the diff view and undo individual AI-run draft edits; and (5) how to share an event page or block Site for review with an optional named approver and how the approval is recorded.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing tracks every change made to a field event's core settings and registration form, so your team always has a full audit trail and a one-click path back to any earlier state. When details change after registration opens, the built-in Details Updated email lets you reach confirmed guests with a clear summary of what changed — with a preview and audience count before anything sends. The version history for AI-built pages shows plain labels, author names, and a live indicator, so reviewers can compare drafts, undo individual edits, and formally approve the version that goes live.
